correctness.rationale: For a single uniform ignition, the expected component size is exactly 1+2 F/n from the pairwise independent path connection probabilities. Every term of F is exp of a linear interval sum; length-one terms force a positive definite Hessian and a unique global budget optimizer. At the proposed symmetric central support, explicit closed gradient differences (m-k)(m q-k) for n=2m and (m-k)(q+m q^2-k) for n=2m+1 give necessary and sufficient KKT conditions, including exact boundaries. The first violated neighbor proves strict suboptimality beyond the threshold, and four-patch strict convexity proves its unique interior continuation. Replayed package checker returns 6952 finite/exact checks; no infinite proof rests solely on computation.

originality.rationale: Nine direct semantic published-finding corpus searches plus published-source and alias searches compared the actual mathematical objective and quantifiers, not titles alone. The closest published exact firebreak paper optimizes two perfect cycle cuts with multiple ignitions, whereas this proves uniquely budgeted probabilistic edge strengths on a singly seeded path; graph-deletion and spatial optimization sources do not entail this special parametric support law. This assessment is conditional on the inspected record and identifies historical-priority residual risk.

value.rationale: The same physically motivated stochastic fire-containment objective has provably different threshold budgets on even versus odd corridors, with a sharp factor-two parity effect, an exact n-family support boundary, and a complete four-patch post-boundary continuation. This distinguishes when concentration in a central fireline ceases to be optimal rather than reporting a numeric optimum in an arbitrary isolated case. The theorem supplies a reproducible analytic benchmark for testing more detailed numerical fire-treatment designs, while clearly disclaiming direct management recommendations.
